messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the person's action to posing for a photo, as demonstrated in the motion reference. Transfer only the demonstrated action; do not adopt the reference person's appearance, the reference scene, or the reference camera setup. Preserve all other aspects of the current video, including the person's identity, appearance, scene, lighting, and camera framing.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please change the person's action to posing for a photo, as demonstrated in the reference video. Transfer only the demonstrated action, not the reference person's appearance or the reference scene and camera setup. Preserve all other aspects of the current video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands in the open area, raises one hand to touch or adjust her hair, then turns slightly to face more toward the camera.","camera":"Static medium-long shot at roughly eye level, framing the character from behind in the center of the scene.","clothing":"She wears a black sleeveless top, light beige wide-leg trousers, and dark open-toed sandals.","hair_color":"White or platinum blonde.","hairstyle":"Hair is pulled back into a high ponytail.","identity":"A 3D-rendered female character with a slim build, seen mostly from behind and in profile.","scene":"An outdoor amusement park at dusk, with a Ferris wheel on the left, a carousel structure with lights on the right, a small kiosk, and a warm sunset sky."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The character now performs a posing sequence: she turns away from the camera, places one hand on her hip, raises the other hand to her hair/head, shifts her weight, and turns back toward the camera. The amusement park scene, sunset lighting, character clothing, hair, and static camera framing remain consistent with the source.
arguments.requested_change: Change the person's action to posing for a photo as shown in the motion reference, while preserving the original character's identity, appearance, scene, lighting, and camera framing.
unexpected_changes: The character's orientation changes from mostly facing the camera in the source to facing away for much of the output, though this is part of the transferred posing motion.
